articles.title: The 3-Team NBA Trade Idea That Would Change Everything
articles.summary: The 2026 NBA offseason's to-do list is dwindling down to almost nothing.
articles.body:
The 2026 NBA offseason's to-do list is dwindling down to almost nothing.

There are still a few things to sort out—an end to Jalen Duren's drawn-out restricted free agency, and perhaps an extension for Stephen Curry—but most of the big-picture decisions have already been made.

We just aren't quite ready for this party to be over.

Maybe we're just guests who are overstaying our welcome, but when you're used to landscape-shifting dominoes being dropped at an almost daily pace, it isn't easy to accept that the activity is just finished. So...we won't.

Instead, we're firing up the trade machine in search of one final summer splash: a three-team blockbuster that could add at least one new franchise to the league's heavyweight contender ranks.

Detroit Pistons receive: Kyrie Irving and Naji Marshall

Golden State Warriors receive: P.J. Washington, Taurean Prince*, 2027 second-round pick (from MIL, via DET) and 2028 second-round pick (from CHO or LAC, via DET)

Dallas Mavericks receive: Ron Holland II, Brandin Podziemski, Daniss Jenkins, Moses Moody, Duncan Robinson and 2028 first-round pick (via DET)

* Eligible to be aggregated in a trade after Sept. 8

Detroit learned two lessons last season. First, this roster is ready to go toe-to-toe with the Association's elite. Teams don't secure 60 wins or post the league's second-best net rating by accident.

Second, the Pistons need to give Cade Cunningham more help to have a realistic shot of capturing the crown. In fact, the need for scoring and creation support might be even greater now than it appeared during the Pistons' second-round exit, since Tobias Harris, their second-leading scorer in the playoffs, has relocated to San Antonio.

The Pistons have managed to snag a few solid additions, but they still need a special kind of co-star for Cunningham. And this deal delivers exactly that in Irving, a historically skilled ball-handler with career averages sitting north of 23 points and five assists (output enhanced by his uber-efficient 47.4/39.4/88.8 career slash line).

Now, the knocks on Irving are obvious—he is 34 years old and spawned significant availability concerns long before suffering the torn ACL that sidelined him all of last season—but the potential reward looms even larger. He has absolutely crushed it as a co-star, winning a championship with LeBron James and helping Luka Dončić secure his first NBA Finals appearance.

Irving could be just as effective with Cunningham, a pairing with enough on-paper potency to settle the spacing concerns tied to having Ausar Thompson and (presumably) Duren in the same frontcourt. Plus, the Pistons acquire a plug-and-play defensive replacement for Ron Holland II in Naji Marshall, a similarly physical defender with a richer inside-the-arc track record on offense.

The long-term costs are hardly insignificant here, but Cunningham's emergence as an All-NBA first-teamer and MVP candidate can justify prioritizing the short term, especially if it means acquiring a proven commodity like Irving without depleting Detroit's draft assets.

The Warriors could soon reward Curry for his epic career and continued excellence with a sizable contract extension. Per ESPN's Anthony Slater , there remains "a mutual desire to keep Curry with the Warriors for the entirety of his career."

Fans might love to see the loyalty here, but couldn't Curry use, you know, some actual on-court support? Granted, Golden State isn't getting back a needle-mover in this exchange, but if that type of upgrade was available to the franchise, it would have signed, sealed and delivered that deal already.

The Warriors haven't ditched their dreams of adding a difference-maker at some point, but this offseason is still in danger of going down as a major drag. They could at least give themselves some proven reinforcements on the wing in P.J. Washington and Taurean Prince while also managing to turn Moses Moody's salary slot into something useful and sidestepping potentially tricky extension talks with Brandin Podziemski.

This deal wouldn't make the Warriors any younger or more athletic, but it would supply more veteran savvy, shotmaking and defensive versatility along the wings. Not to mention, Washington and Prince would arrive with nearly 50 combined playoff appearances on their résumés.

Washington would be a rotation regular (if not a nightly starter, at least until Jimmy Butler returns), while Prince's role could hinge on the readiness of first-round rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. Neither newcomer would change the Warriors' fate, but they could beef up the rotation a bit without subtracting any draft assets (and, in fact, adding a couple of seconds to perhaps sweeten a future trade offer).

That feels like a solid bit of basketball business, especially if there are any hesitations about Podziemski's next contract or Moody's status after suffering a gruesome knee injury late last season.

When given the opportunity, Dallas keeps arguing for Irving as a viable co-star for Cooper Flagg. Rival franchises just aren't buying it and "continue to wonder aloud about how firmly Dallas will stick to that stance," per NBA insider Marc Stein .

That skepticism is absolutely warranted. It's arguably encouraged given the gargantuan timeline gap between the 34-year-old Irving and 19-year-old Flagg.

Speaking of the reigning Rookie of the Year, how is he feeling about the state of long-term building blocks around him? First-round rookies Morez Johnson Jr. and Sergio de Larrea might be the two most exciting options, but that says plenty when they have collectively proved nothing at this level. Optimists might add a hopefully healthy Dereck Lively II and 2024's No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher to the list, but they'd have their fingers tightly crossed while doing it.

What really ups the concern factor, though, is that Dallas doesn't own any of its next four first-round draft picks. So, there isn't an obvious (or easy) way of adding to his young core. Unless, of course, the Mavs reverse course on their Irving stance, which feels like it could happen as soon as the front office senses a respectable return is available on the draft market.

This would almost certainly qualify. Dallas could hold realistic hopes of landing four long-term keepers here, since Ron Holland II, Brandin Podziemski, Daniss Jenkins and Moses Moody are all 25 or under. And if the front office aced the incoming first-round pick, that would be five fresh building blocks in place—plus Duncan Robinson, who'd bring valuable offensive spacing and hopefully convince a shooting-needy suitor to come calling at some point.

That is, without question, a healthy haul for a 34-year-old returning from a season-long absence and a couple of veteran role players. More importantly, it is a clear and complete commitment to prioritizing Flagg's future, which became (or at least should have become) the organization's first priority the second it collected the jackpot prize of the 2025 draft lottery.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards' Reaction to Kuminga Contract, LaMelo Trade, Wolves Deals Revealed in New NBA Rumors
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves superstar guard Anthony Edwards is reportedly satisfied with the moves the front office has made this offseason.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves superstar guard Anthony Edwards is reportedly satisfied with the moves the front office has made this offseason.

Speaking Friday during the Brian Windhorst & The Hoop Collective podcast (beginning at the 9:30 mark) , ESPN NBA insider Brian Windhorst said, "From what I understand, Ant was very excited. Ant, from what I am told, is very pleased by the Wolves' offseason."

Minnesota's most notable moves this offseason included signing Ayo Dosunmu to a contract extension, acquiring guard LaMelo Ball from the Charlotte Hornets in a trade that sent Naz Reid and draft picks to Charlotte, and signing forward Jonathan Kuminga to a two-year, $12.43 million deal this week.

The T'Wolves have reached the playoffs in five consecutive seasons and won at least one playoff series in each of the past three years, but they have been unable to get over the hump and into the NBA Finals.

After falling in the Western Conference Finals in both 2024 and 2025, Minnesota was eliminated in the second round last season, falling 4-2 to the San Antonio Spurs.

As a result, president of basketball operations Tim Connelly made the decision to shake things up by parting with Reid and three-time All-Star forward Julius Randle in favor of Ball and Kuminga.

With a projected starting lineup of Edwards, Ball, Dosunmu, Kuminga and Rudy Gobert, plus Jaden McDaniels and Donte DiVincenzo coming off the bench, the Timberwolves look to have one of the deepest rosters in the NBA.

They also have a bona fide MVP candidate in Edwards, who has shown improvement in each of his six NBA seasons since getting selected first overall in 2020.

Edwards averaged a career-high 28.8 points per game last season, and the four-time All-Star could have an even higher scoring ceiling during the 2026-27 campaign with Ball as a distributor.

Ultimately, the Timberwolves need for Edwards to be happy and for the roster construction to work since he has three years left on his deal, and a potential trade is something that could come into focus as soon as next year if things don't work out.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball Trade Called 'Significant Gamble' in NBA, New Wolves Rumors Leak After Kuminga Contract
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves' offseason acquisition of guard LaMelo Ball is reportedly being met with skepticism inside NBA circles.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves' offseason acquisition of guard LaMelo Ball is reportedly being met with skepticism inside NBA circles.

During a discussion Friday on Brian Windhorst & The Hoop Collective (beginning at the 12-minute mark) , ESPN NBA insider Tim MacMahon said, "If we're being honest, there's more optimism, I think, from fans about LaMelo going to Minnesota than there is out of front offices around the league. This was looked at as a significant gamble by [T'Wolves president of basketball operations] Tim Connelly, who's known as a riverboat gambler."

Trade Idea That Would Change Everything 💡💡

Connelly took a big swing last month by acquiring Ball and Josh Green from the Charlotte Hornets in exchange for Naz Reid, a 2033 first-round pick, three second-round picks and three future pick swaps.

Minnesota also sent three-time All-Star forward Julius Randle to the Brooklyn Nets in a salary dump as part of the deal.

Ball was the centerpiece of a busy offseason for the Timberwolves, as they also signed Ayo Dosunmu to a contract extension and signed forward Jonathan Kuminga in free agency this week.

Originally selected third overall by the Hornets in the 2020 NBA draft, Ball burst onto the scene, winning NBA Rookie of the Year honors.

He followed that up the next season with his first and only All-Star selection, averaging 20.1 points, 7.6 assists and 6.7 rebounds per game.

On paper, Ball had great production over his six seasons in Charlotte, putting up 20.8 points, 7.3 assists, 5.7 rebounds, 3.2 three-pointers made and 1.4 steals per contest.

However, he has never been a particularly efficient player, shooting just 41.8 percent from the field in his career, and turning the ball over 3.2 times per game on average.

Because of that, there have been questions about whether Ball is a winning basketball player. After all, the Hornets never reached the playoffs during his tenure with the team.

On top of that, durability has been a concern with Ball, as he has played in 51 or fewer games in four of his six NBA seasons.

He was an All-Star when he played in a career-high 75 games in 2021-22, though, and he did manage to appear in 72 games last season.

Perhaps the biggest gamble of all when it comes to the Timberwolves landing Ball is rolling the dice on how he will mesh on the court with superstar guard Anthony Edwards.

Both Edwards and Ball are ball-dominant players, but it is unquestionably Edwards' team, as he has been named an All-Star each of the past four seasons and averaged 28.8 points per game last season.

Edwards is the driving force behind Minnesota's success, and the team needs Ball to be a quality complement rather than a player who adversely impacts what Edwards is trying to do.

It remains to be seen if Ball can be that type of player, but if he can, then he could prove to be a steal and the missing piece that helps the Timberwolves get over the top and into the NBA Finals.

articles.title: NBA 2K27 Is Making Major Upgrades to Both Ends of the Court
articles.body:
Let's be honest, the NBA offseason has already thrown up enough plot twists to fill a MyCAREER cutscene. LeBron James scooting off to Philly, the Lakers embroiled in an ownership drama involving a reported $12.5 billion valuation, and Victor Wembanyama going from basketball's terrifyingly talented alien to the face of NBA 2K27. The 2026-27 season hasn't even tipped off yet, and I'm already calling for a timeout.

Fortunately, there's a new NBA 2K on the way to keep me occupied. After the franchise's big preseason reveal dropped details across virtually every mode, here's my vibe check on what my fellow hoopers should be psyched for most.

Gameplay wants to play both ends of the floor

NBA 2K27 is making a pretty convincing case that this year's biggest changes aren't about finding one overpowered move and spamming it until my opponent rage-quits. The offensive side of the ball gets new toys including step-through up-and-unders, a Dynamic Layup Engine and expanded dribbling customisation, giving me more control over how I create space and attack the rim.

Defence isn't parking its arse on the bench either. Hands-up defence has been redesigned, the shot contest system has been overhauled, defensive cutoffs have been expanded and a new collision system should give physical play more weight. In other words, NBA 2K27 is trying to make both ends of the court count, which sounds like good news for anyone who has ever watched a teammate sprint towards the three-point line and decide defence is somebody else's problem.

MyCAREER is getting a particularly juicy addition this year, with five playable eras allowing me to build a basketball career across different points in NBA history. Quick e.g.: I can start in the Magic vs. Bird Era of 1984 and work through the decades, all the way to the Steph Era of 2016. Nice.

Then there's Fire & Concrete, an 11-chapter cinematic story featuring rapper and actor Vince Staples. That's more than twice the length of last year's story, so there should be considerably more time for my MyPLAYER to make questionable life choices while looking suspiciously good in expensive digital clothing.

Even better, NBA 2K27 introduces co-op MyCAREER for the first time. A friend can join my career through Running Mate Trace Miller, meaning I can finally share the grind instead of merely arguing about whose build is broken in the group chat.

MyPLAYERs to compete together across the City's activities.

Crew players also get a new home with Crew HQ, which provides dedicated space for practice, ranked competition, private games, Crew progression and seasonal tournaments. Meanwhile, the City itself has been refreshed with new environments and activities including Rucker Park in Street Kings, Casual Corner and Daily Rivals.

With 40 REP tiers available at launch, there should be plenty of incentive to keep grinding. I'll just have to remember that the sun does eventually come up, no matter how convincing the "one more game" argument sounds at 2:47am.

If my idea of fun involves less ankle-breaking and more spreadsheets, MyNBA is stepping back onto the court with a back-to-basics overhaul. The mode is getting more focus on its foundational franchise systems, including realistic CBA contract negotiations and a new GM Trust system that should make my decisions carry more weight.

Then things get properly ambitious with MyNBA Legacy. This new single-player RPG-style experience lets me run a franchise from the front office while also dominating on the court as the same locked player, with the franchise window stretching across an enormous 100 years. That's enough time to build a dynasty, destroy it, rebuild it and then wonder why I gave that one centre a seven-year contract.

MyTEAM is also getting some major progression changes. The Exchange will now accept any Player Card in my collection, giving those cards gathering virtual dust at the back of my lineup another shot at contributing to the cause.

An all-new Player XP system will let every Player Card level up and unlock rewards, while rotating multiplayer modes, a unified Auction House, new Player Card Parallels and expanded Breakout progression add more ways to build, upgrade and play with my dream NBA and WNBA lineups.

NBA 2K27 is giving its WNBA modes more room to run, too. The W and MyWNBA both receive dedicated single-player experiences, alongside a Build-as-You-Go progression system, an updated Game Attribute System and new Team Badges and Teammate Badges.

Those badges are designed to build chemistry and give me two distinct upgrade paths, while MyWNBA adds more tools for running a WNBA franchise from the front office. It's another sign that NBA 2K27 is treating its various forms of basketball as more than just different courts sharing the same ball.

Perhaps the slickest quality-of-life addition is the new NBA 2K HQ companion app, which went live August 21. It lets you build and edit MyPLAYERs on the go before uploading those builds directly to my console, while QR-code sharing makes it easier to send builds to friends. The app also handles real-time messaging, Crew management, leaderboards and mobile-exclusive daily rewards. So even when I'm away from the console, the grind doesn't have to ride the pine.

Taken together, NBA 2K27 looks like a game that's trying to give every kind of hooper a reason to check back in. Whether I want to recreate basketball history, build a MyPLAYER, run a century-long franchise, collect cards, dominate The City or simply jump online with friends, there's a sizable menu of new plays to run.

And with the real NBA coming off an offseason featuring LeBron's move to Philly, the Lakers' ownership saga and a schedule that already has a Finals rematch lined up for Christmas Day, there's no shortage of inspiration.

NBA 2K27 tips off September 4, with Deluxe and Ultra Edition players getting an early start from August 27.

articles.title: Career turning point: “When I started knocking down my three’s, it just felt right”: How Sophie Cunningham’s 42-point night at Missouri changed the course of her career forever
articles.summary: NBA News: Sophie Cunningham had already made plenty of noise before she ever played a college game. The Columbia, Missouri, native was a four-time state champio.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham had already made plenty of noise before she ever played a college game. The Columbia, Missouri, native was a four-time state champion at Rock Bridge and one of the country's most respected high school recruits. She knew what it felt like to carry expectations. What she did not know yet was how quickly she could make the jump to college basketball. That answer came much sooner than anyone expected.Just four games into her freshman season at Missouri, Cunningham went off against Wake Forest for 42 points. She shot 13-of-18 from the floor, knocked down six threes and added eight rebounds, four assists and three steals. More importantly, she broke a Missouri scoring record that had stood since 1986. She did not even know she was closing in on the record. She was simply playing, finding her rhythm and taking the shots that were there. That night changed the way Missouri saw its freshman and became the first major step toward the career she would eventually build. Why was the Wake Forest game the turning point in Sophie Cunningham’s career?There was already plenty to like about Cunningham when she arrived at Missouri. She was not some overlooked recruit who suddenly appeared out of nowhere. Her high school career had made sure of that. At Rock Bridge High School, she helped win four consecutive Missouri Class 5 state championships and finished with 1,983 career points. She earned the 2014 USA Today Gatorade Missouri Girls Basketball Player of the Year award and later played in the McDonald's All-American Game.Still, none of that told Missouri exactly what it had in her. High school success can create expectations, but college basketball is where those expectations have to be tested. Cunningham had to adjust to bigger, stronger defenders and a faster game while learning how to play alongside experienced college players.She had only three games to begin that adjustment before Wake Forest came to town.The game quickly turned into Cunningham's night. She scored 25 points in the first half and went 9-of-10 from the field during those opening 20 minutes. Four of her five three-point attempts went in before halftime. She kept attacking after the break and finished with 42 points in Missouri's 94-81 victory.The number immediately stood out. Forty-two points meant Cunningham had broken Missouri's single-game scoring record. The previous mark was 41, set by Renee Kelly in 1986. Cunningham had surpassed it less than a month into her college career.What makes the moment more convincing as a turning point is what Cunningham said afterward. She was not talking about making history or trying to establish herself as Missouri's next star. She was talking about winning.“Honestly, when I’m playing out there on the court I don’t think about that kind of stuff. I’m just trying to do what it takes to win, and my teammates did a great job of getting me the ball when I needed it and setting me up for screens and stuff, so really props to them for getting me the ball last night,” Cunningham said.That was Cunningham's first major college statement, even if she did not treat it that way. She had shown she could take over a game without getting caught up in the moment. Missouri had a freshman who could score in bunches, handle pressure and still keep her attention on the team. That was a pretty important discovery.How did Sophie Cunningham’s breakout performance change her path at Missouri?The Wake Forest game would have been a fun story even if Cunningham had never reached the same level again. A freshman scoring 42 points and breaking a decades-old record is memorable on its own. But Cunningham made sure it was not a one-night thing.She finished her freshman season averaging 14.0 points, 5.8 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game. She shot 50.2% from the field and earned SEC Freshman of the Year honors. Suddenly, the expectations surrounding her were no longer based only on what she had done at Rock Bridge. Now there was college production to support them.The three-point shooting from the Wake Forest game also became an important part of her identity. Cunningham had found something that night, and she knew exactly when it started clicking.“When I started knocking down my three’s, it just felt right,” Cunningham said.She added that she did not realize how many points she had scored during the game and did not even know she was approaching the record. That detail says a lot about how naturally the night unfolded. She was not hunting for 42. She was simply playing with confidence, and once the shots started dropping, Wake Forest struggled to slow her down.There was another layer to the performance, too. Cunningham was dealing with an ankle issue, but she continued to compete through the physical game. Missouri coach Robin Pingeton praised her toughness and competitiveness afterward. For a freshman, that mattered. She was beginning to show that she could contribute even when everything was not comfortable.From there, Cunningham's role at Missouri only grew.She became a three-time All-SEC First Team selection and finished her college career with 2,187 points. That made her Missouri's all-time leading scorer. She also finished with 706 made field goals, 238 three-pointers, 537 free throws and 390 assists. Missouri reached the NCAA Tournament in all four of her seasons.Those achievements put the Wake Forest performance into a different context. It was not the best game of a player whose career eventually faded. It was the opening chapter of a much bigger rise.Her senior season showed just how much her game had expanded. Cunningham became the only player in the country that season to average at least 17 points, 200 rebounds, 80 three-pointers and 150 free throws. The player who had first turned heads with a scoring explosion had developed into a much more complete offensive weapon.The record against Wake Forest was still there, sitting at the start of it all. What did her early success eventually mean for her WNBA career?By the time Sophie Cunningham left Missouri, she had gone from highly rated recruit to program legend. The next question was whether that success could translate to the professional level.The Phoenix Mercury gave her that opportunity when they selected her 13th overall in the 2019 WNBA Draft. Her role changed almost immediately. At Missouri, Cunningham had been one of the team's primary scoring options. In the WNBA, she had to learn how to make an impact without needing the ball in her hands all the time.That adjustment became an important part of her professional development. Her shooting remained valuable, but she also brought physicality, energy and the willingness to do the less glamorous work. She spent her first six WNBA seasons with Phoenix and gradually became a dependable veteran presence.Her move to Indiana opened another chapter. Cunningham joined the Fever in January 2025 as part of a four-team trade and became a useful piece of the rotation. She helped Indiana win the 2025 Commissioner's Cup and scored 13 points in the championship game.The setting was very different from that night against Wake Forest, but some things had not changed. Cunningham was still the player who wanted to compete, take open shots and do whatever the team needed.That mindset was already visible after her record-breaking freshman performance. Instead of making the night about herself, Cunningham talked about what Missouri could accomplish together.“This year is going to be outstanding. We have very versatile players here. We have all the puzzle pieces we need and so if we can just put that puzzle together it’s going to be a huge year for Mizzou women’s basketball,” she said.The quote feels different when viewed with the benefit of hindsight. Cunningham was still only a freshman, but she was already thinking beyond one performance. She wanted the record to mean something for the team, not simply for herself.That is ultimately why the Wake Forest game stands out as the real turning point in her early career. It did not magically turn Cunningham into a WNBA player. Her later success came from years of development, consistency and adapting to different roles. But the 42-point night gave her the first undeniable proof that she could take her game to another level.She arrived at Missouri as a decorated high school player with a lot to prove. Four games later, she owned a school scoring record.The record eventually became just one line in a much longer resume. Cunningham went on to become Missouri's all-time leading scorer, a WNBA draft pick and a veteran capable of contributing in different roles.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: El club blanco acaba de anunciar la contratación del pívot estadounidense dos veces campeón de la NBA, que queda vinculado hasta 2027
articles.summary: El club blanco acaba de anunciar la contratación del pívot estadounidense dos veces campeón de la NBA, que queda vinculado hasta
articles.body: El Real Madrid va cerrando poco a poco su plantilla de cara al próximo curso. Después de oficializar la última contratación de Olivier Sarr, ahora el club se ha movido para encontrar un sustituto de garantías para dar descanso a Tavares. Damian Jones, jugador de 2,08 metros de altura y 31 años de edad, es el elegido. Firma por una temporada. El pívot, tras su periplo en estos últimos dos años China y Puerto Rico, donde ha jugado en esta última edición de la Liga de Verano. llega ahora a una entidad que necesita de su contundencia bajo el aro y sus recursos novedosos desde el exterior. Llega un pívot plagado de experiencia en la mejor liga del mundo, la NBA: ganó dos anillos de campeón de la NBA con los Golden State Warriors (2016/17 y 2017/18), aunque su participación fue testimonial. Tras su ciclo en San Francisco, su protagonismo fue a más en los Atlanta Hawks, aunque volvió a decrecer en los Phoenix Suns y Los Ángeles Lakers. Su mejor nivel en la liga norteamericana llegó en 2021, cuando firmó con los Sacramento Kings. Su fichaje provocó la mejor versión del pívot, que llegó a promediar 8,1 puntos y 4,4 rebotes en 56 partidos. Sin embargo, después de pasar por Utah y por Cleveland, donde promedió 2,7 puntos y 1,6 rebotes en 7 minutos por partido, al pívot se le acabó su estancia en la liga de una forma no muy deseada. Tras emigrar de Estados Unidos, Jones recaló en los Zhejiang Golden Bulls, donde logró promediar 17,7 puntos, 9,1 rebotes y dos tapones por partido en la 24/25.Unos números que bajaron en la pasada campaña 25/26, en la que terminó con 9,7 puntos, 5,7 rebotes y tapón y medio por aparición en la competición doméstica asiática. Sin embargo, cabe destacar su crecimiento en el tiro exterior, donde acabó con un 41,2% y un 38,2% respectivamente en sus años en China. Este mismo verano, el pívot ha disputado la liga puertorriqueña con los Vaqueros de Bayamón, promediando 13 puntos (firmando un 81% de acierto en tiros de campo) 5,7 rebotes, 1,2 asistencias y 2,5 tapones en 10 apariciones en el país centroamericano. Con esta incorporación, Damian Jones se convierte en el cuarto pívot en tres temporadas (sin contar a Yurtseven y Sissoko, que llegaron a Madrid por causas excepcionales) para suplir a Tavares. Desde 2019, solo un pívot ha conseguido adaptarse a ese rol: Vincent Poirier, cuya vuelta a la capital española este verano parecía posible hasta la grave lesión sufrida en el tendón de Aquiles en los playoff de la liga turca en mayo de 2026. El francés, que se marchó en 2024 al Anadolu Efes, dejó un vacío enorme que aun no ha sido ocupado: Serge Ibaka, Bruno Fernando y Alex Len han sido tres apuestas para intentar suplirle y ninguno de ellos se ha acercado mínimamente a lo aportado por el galo. Ya fuese por falta de oportunidades o carencia de nivel, ninguno ha conseguido tapar la sombra de Poirier, algo que intentará hacer Jones en este próximo año. Damian Jones, de Baton Rouge, Luisiana, ocupará plaza de extracomunitario. El Madrid ya no tiene problemas con esto tras conseguir el pasaporte español Gaby Deck. Chuma Okeke es el otro 'americano' de la plantilla.

articles.title: Enes Freedom vs Natasha Cloud: The opposing activists at the center of the WNBA's latest signature moment
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud's courtside altercation during a Chicago Sky game drew 3.31 million viewers and sparked a ban and legal threats.
articles.body: Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud just couldn't help themselves. The duo gave the WNBA its closest equivalent to the "Malice in The Palace" incident on Sunday night, and the Chicago Sky turned it into a week of news with a ban and an interview. Here's how activism set both Freedom and Cloud on a collision course into sports hysteria: ENES KANTER FREEDOM OPENS UP ON CONFRONTATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD THAT LED TO EJECTION, WNBA PURSUIT Two different definitions of freedom They came from opposite ends of the world. Freedom built his public identity fighting governments abroad. Cloud built hers challenging institutions here in the U.S. Both came to see an athlete’s platform as an obligation. Both became comfortable with confrontation. But they developed nearly opposite definitions of who needed protection and what posed the threat. Freedom’s activism came first, and it came with consequences. Born in Switzerland and raised in Turkey, Freedom moved to the United States as a teenager and became the third overall pick in the 2011 NBA Draft. Basketball gave him a career. Turkey gave him a cause. Freedom traces his political awakening to 2013, when corruption allegations engulfed the government of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. He became an outspoken Erdoğan critic and a prominent supporter of Fethullah Gülen, the U.S.-based cleric whom Turkey blamed for the failed 2016 coup attempt. Freedom accused Erdoğan’s government of crushing dissent, jailing journalists and using terrorism charges against political opponents. His criticism eventually made a return to Turkey unsafe. Then the conflict reached his family. Freedom’s relatives publicly disowned him as pressure mounted. His father lost his university job, faced prosecution on terrorism charges and was eventually acquitted. Turkish authorities canceled Freedom’s passport in 2017, leaving him temporarily detained at a Romanian airport during an international charity tour. He later skipped NBA travel outside the United States because he feared detention or forced return to Turkey. Freedom received U.S. citizenship in 2021 and legally added Freedom to his name. His advocated for speech without government retaliation, religion without persecution and dissent without prison. America, in his telling, was special to him because it allowed the criticism that authoritarian countries punished. Then during the 2021-22 NBA season, Freedom wore custom shoes highlighting China’s treatment of Tibetans and Uyghur Muslims. He promoted Hong Kong and Taiwanese autonomy, attacked forced labor and accused the NBA, Nike and prominent players of muting criticism to protect business interests in China. A Chinese streaming service stopped showing Boston Celtics games after his first Free Tibet demonstration. Freedom continued anyway. Meanwhile, Cloud, during her upbringing, enjoyed many of the American liberties that Freedom did not when he was growing up. She was raised in a predominantly White family in Broomall, Pennsylvania. Cloud entered the WNBA in 2015 and joined a league already more politically outspoken than most American sports institutions. By 2016, she was participating in the Washington Mystics’ protest of the police shootings of Alton Sterling and Philando Castile. The Mystics wore "Black Lives Matter" shirts and joined a media blackout intended to pressure the league. WNBA PLAYER NATASHA CLOUD FIRES OFF PRO-TRANS MESSAGE FOLLOWING ALTERCATION WITH ENES KANTER FREEDOM In 2019, two shootings near Hendley Elementary School forced children into lockdown twice in two weeks. The school sat less than two miles from the Mystics’ arena in Southeast Washington. Cloud responded by pressing city leaders for action and temporarily refusing to discuss basketball with reporters. She turned the team’s media availability into a campaign for school safety and sustained investment in Ward 8. Her advocacy expanded into a broader effort against gun violence. The Mystics won the WNBA championship later that year. But Cloud walked away from the title defense. After George Floyd’s death in 2020, Cloud opted out of the entire WNBA season to work on racial-justice initiatives. She helped lead marches, promoted voter registration and pushed for the Mystics’ arena to serve as a polling location. Converse supported the decision and covered the salary she forfeited. The WNBA later presented the choice as the defining turn in her development as an activist. Cloud’s cause became broad but consistent. Racial justice. Police accountability. Gun control. Voting access. LGBTQ rights. Investment in women’s sports. Thus, they naturally ended up on opposite sides of the transgender debate. Freedom sees the female category as a protected boundary that gender ideology threatens to dissolve. Cloud sees transgender people as part of a broader community that political movements have targeted. He frames his campaign as a defense of women. She frames opposition to transgender inclusion as another attack on a vulnerable group. Their first collision came online Freedom and Cloud did not need a courtside seat to find each other the first time. Their first major public clash came in July 2023, when Cloud criticized the United States against the backdrop of Supreme Court rulings affecting affirmative action and LGBTQ rights. "Our country is trash in so many ways and instead of using our resources to make it better we continue to oppress Marginalized groups that we have targeted since the beginning of times. Black/brown communities & LGBTQ+ man we are too powerful to still be attacking issues separate," Cloud wrote on social media at the time. Freedom responded, writing "Just ask your colleague Brittney Griner how ‘trash’ America is. Calling America trash huh? Let me know when your season is over…" as Griner's detention in a Russian prison had been a national storyline that year. Cloud responded more diplomatically then than she did on Sunday. "I have respect for @EnesFreedom lived experience in his country," Cloud wrote. "I would expect him to have the same respect for MY lived experience as a black gay woman in my country." Freedom recalled the incident in a recent interview with OutKick. "Me and Natasha Cloud got into it back in 2023, and not many people know about it, when she called America trash," Freedom said. "When people have no idea what the other side looks like, they can call America anything that they want, but it was unacceptable, so I checked her on that one." The incident At 2:31 p.m on Sunday., Freedom’s manager, Hank Fetic, texted Sky general manager Jeff Pagliocca to say they would be at the game. The message, obtained by OutKick, said Pagliocca had "always been fair" and "deserved a heads up in advance." "Enes and I will be at the sky game tonight," Fetic wrote. Pagliocca responded at 5:30 p.m., approximately 30 minutes before tipoff: "Appreciate the text, hope you are well too." Sky principal owner Michael Alter told OutKick that he and his team considered the phrase "deserved a heads up" a warning that Freedom planned to do more than watch basketball. "When you say you deserve to know, why would you say you deserve to know?" Alter said. "That’s a clear, direct indication that be ready, trouble’s coming." Alter said organization alerted security but allowed Freedom inside. Alter said staff members were instructed to ignore him and not "take the bait." But Alter said the players were not told he was coming, a decision he admitted he regretted. That decision resulted in consequences in the third quarter, when Cloud initiated a now-infamous altercation. Freedom said Cloud first turned toward him and said, "She’s not going to sleep with you," in response to him cheering for Sophie Cunningham. Freedom said he responded that he was not trying to sleep with Cunningham and was there to support her and "protect women." According to Freedom, Cloud answered with repeated profanity. "She started to drop a lot of F-bombs, and she started to curse a lot, and she started to bark at me," Freedom said. "I’m like, ‘There are lots of kids and teenage girls in the stands idolizing you. This is unacceptable.’" With 1:22 remaining in the third quarter, Cloud scored inside before a timeout, chest-bumped teammate Aicha Coulibaly and walked in Freedom’s direction. Video shows Cloud yelling and pointing as she approached the baseline. Freedom stood, extended his arms, gestured toward Cloud and stepped forward. Security arrived almost immediately while teammates and staff restrained Cloud. Freedom was ejected. Cloud remained in the game and there is no public knowledge of any discipline assigned to her. The Sky said Wintrust Arena security, NBA Security and Chicago police determined that Freedom became a potential threat when he opened his arms, pointed at Cloud and moved toward the playing surface. In a written response obtained by OutKick, the organization said WNBA officials agreed with the decision and would have demanded Freedom’s removal if security had returned him to his seat. Alter said the response was remarkably fast. "It was the quickest decision I’ve ever seen in someone being ejected from a game," he said. But Alter acknowledged that he did not know whether Freedom crossed the baseline. He had not reviewed the officials’ written report and did not possess documentation showing that Chicago police made a separate threat assessment. No report or direct statement from the security entities identified by the Sky has been publicly released. "I can’t tell you what his intent was beyond his actions," Alter said. "I don’t know what was in his head." Freedom insisted there was nothing more in his head—or in his feet. "That was my last step," he said. "I’m telling you right now, I was not gonna take another step. I was gonna stop there." Freedom argued that 11 years in the NBA had taught him where a spectator could and could not stand. "If I step over the baseline, yes, they have every right to throw me out of the game," he said. "I literally simply opened my arms and said, ‘I’m here to protect women.’" The written rules settle more of the warning dispute. Freedom repeatedly argued that security was required to warn him before ejecting him. The WNBA Fan Code of Conduct, however, says guests who fight, throw objects or attempt to enter the court will be "immediately ejected." It does not require a warning for that offense and expressly permits future-game bans. A warning provision does appear in the 2026 WNBA Official Rule Book, but under the narrower category of "Verbal Fan Interference." It applies when verbal abuse interferes with a coach’s ability to communicate with players during a game or huddle. Freedom would have been entitled to a warning under that provision before an ejection for continued verbal interference. If security reasonably determined that he attempted to enter the court, immediate removal was permitted. Alter defended that distinction with the interview’s most incendiary line. "He wasn’t given a warning because certain threats don’t get warnings," Alter said. "To use an extreme example, when you shoot a gun at someone, you don’t get a warning, ‘Don’t do that again.’" Meanwhile, the WNBA rulebook identifies profanity and taunting as unsportsmanlike conduct that can warrant a technical foul. The available evidence does not establish Cloud’s exact language, whether officials heard the alleged profanity or whether her actions required any automatic penalty. But Freedom thinks she should be fined and required to review the league’s player-conduct rules. "Of course, obviously, as an owner, he’s gonna try to do whatever he can to protect his player," Freedom said. "But she should be disciplined for sure." Alter repeatedly declined to say whether Cloud will be penalized while speaking to OutKick. Cloud did not give reporters a detailed account. She instead returned to the political subject online, posting a message of support for transgender people after the game. Sky coach Tyler Marsh defended her as someone who protects her teammates and "people that need to be protected." The Fever won 113-90. Freedom displayed his shirt to the crowd while security escorted him away, spoke with police in the arena lobby and posted that he had been ejected "for supporting WOMEN." Cloud remained with the Sky and spoke with team and league security after the game. Then the organization extended the incident beyond Sunday. Alter announced Tuesday that Freedom was banned from future Sky games at Wintrust Arena unless he could prove that he understood the rules and would no longer present a potential threat. Alter did not identify a formal reinstatement process or explain exactly what Freedom would need to do. "I’m not going to give him a roadmap," Alter said. On Wednesday, Freedom sent a formal letter to WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert that OutKick obtained. He requested an explanation for his ejection, a review of Cloud’s conduct, a refund for his tickets and preservation of arena video, security reports and internal communications. He also asked whether his shirt, advocacy or announced effort to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft influenced the decision. The letter accused the league of selective enforcement and cited other recent security controversies involving messages about transgender participation in women’s sports. One week before the Chicago game, the WNBA acknowledged that security at an Atlanta Dream game acted improperly by directing fans to cover shirts carrying messages on both sides of that debate. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "This should not have happened," the league said afterward. The Sky denied that Freedom’s viewpoint or clothing caused his removal. That explanation is supported by the fact that the organization knew he was coming, admitted him in the shirt and allowed him to remain courtside for more than two quarters. Its stated line was the step toward the court. Freedom’s letter nevertheless demanded a written response within five business days. A day later, after hearing Alter’s gun analogy, Freedom raised the stakes again. "Me and my legal team will definitely be taking actions against Chicago Sky and Michael Alter," Freedom said in Wednesday's interview with OutKick. Freedom did not identify a legal claim or provide a filing timeline. The incident and its fallout may have yielded the WNBA and the Sky another PR headache, but also profit. The game averaged 3.31 million viewers across NBC and Peacock and peaked at 3.82 million, making it the most-watched WNBA regular-season game since the league’s opening weekend in 1997 and the third-most watched ever.

articles.title: Latest Buzz on Steph Curry's Decision on Contract Extension from Top Warriors Insider
articles.summary: Stephen Curry could create a "lingering distraction" if he chooses to hold off on signing an extension with the Golden State Warriors despite being unlikely to do so, according to Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry could create a "lingering distraction" if he chooses to hold off on signing an extension with the Golden State Warriors despite being unlikely to do so, according to Nick Friedell of The Athletic.

"The overwhelming likelihood has always been that Curry will sign and the Warriors will go about business as usual, with him as the focal point of everything they do," Friedell reported Friday. "But if he waits, whether as a statement about the roster or simply because he wants to see what happens next, the uncertainty would create the type of lingering distraction that will hover over the group until there is resolution."

On Saturday, Curry will become eligible to sign a two-year extension worth $136.7 million with the Warriors (h/t ESPN's Bobby Marks ).

The two-time MVP is currently set to receive $62.6 million for the 2026-27 season before hitting free agency next summer.

Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy previously expressed confidence in reaching an extension agreement with Curry.

"I'm pretty confident Steph will finish his career (with the Warriors)," Dunleavy said on Aug. 11, per ESPN's Anthony Slater . "Ultimately it's his call, his decision, whether that's allowing his contract to run out and move on or — look, if he comes to me and wants to be moved, Joe and I will talk it through. We wouldn't love it. But he's earned the right to do what he wants. But as far as the messaging or any idea that he'd be anywhere else, that's not a thing we're looking at or he's looking at."

After wrapping up a 37-45 finish last season, the Warriors brought back several free agents including Draymond Green, Kristaps Porziņģis, Al Horford, De'Anthony Melton and Gary Payton II.

Golden State didn't make many notable external moves, as the team reportedly attempted to land LeBron James in free agency before he ultimately joined the Philadelphia 76ers.

It's also worth noting that Warriors wings Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are both recovering from season-ending injuries .

If Curry isn't confident that Golden State can climb up the Western Conference standings, the 38-year-old may choose to wait before signing an extension.

articles.title: Matt Rhule sounds alarm on NFL returnees, $45 million rosters and college football’s payroll problem
articles.summary: Nebraska's Matt Rhule reveals playoff teams are spending about $45 million on player payroll, saying the term NIL no longer applies to college football.
articles.body: The debate over whether NFL returnees should be allowed back into college athletics isn’t going away anytime soon, especially with the amount of court proceedings taking place amid new conference guidelines. Over the past few months, dozens of lawsuits have been filed across the country challenging the eligibility rules for athletes from the 2022 class. What began as a fight over an additional year of eligibility has now turned into a full-blown battle involving conferences, schools, attorneys and state court judges. GOVERNOR LANDRY BACKS LANE KIFFIN, LSU IN FIGHT WITH SEC: 'DON'T HATE THE PLAYER, HATE THE GAME' The fallout has led conferences across college athletics to enact new guidelines outlining potential punishments for schools that roster plaintiffs granted an injunction or temporary restraining order by a local judge. In Louisiana and Texas alone over the past week, more than 50 athletes have been granted another year of eligibility. Attorneys are now adding conferences, including the SEC, to their lawsuits because of the new guidelines meant to deter schools from taking these players. Athletes with NFL training camp experience returning to college are better One of the more interesting debates around this entire saga has centered around the competitive advantage these athletes would have on the field. While some might wonder how much better a fourth string player participating in NFL camp would actually be with a return to college, Nebraska's Matt Rhule told OutKick's Dan Dakich that these athletes would have a considerate advantage over players who have been practicing on a college campus. "Twice as good, twice as good," Rhule told Dakich. "I mean, I think the hardest thing, you know, when you're coaching these guys is you're always telling them like, 'hey guys, do this, this is what it's like, or the next level'. You know, half of it is like as a kid, you know they’re kids, right?...Like just the growth you make. "They train for the combine. They train in a pro facility, had an agent pay for their meals, trained with NFL teams, they had training camp...I think if an NFL player came back, it would be twice, if not three times better than they were." Whether or not you believe that is a entirely different topic of discussion, but I think most would take the word of the Nebraska head coach. LSU’S LANE KIFFIN FIRES BACK AT NFL RETURNEE BACKLASH: BLAME THE NCAA, NOT US FOR RECRUITING PRO ATHLETES Though, maybe he's just saying this to create fear for judges across the country. This is just 'player payroll' now in college football, not NIL or rev-share We are essentially living in an era where college sports should be viewed more like Double-A baseball than the amateur model administrators spent decades trying to protect. Better yet, think of how much it will cost these schools to continue fielding a roster that is in the CFP conversation when the first week of November comes around. As for the entire "name, image and likeness" conversation, Rhule says that is no longer the proper way to describe how college athletes are being compensated. "People use the term NIL for a while. We gotta get rid of that, it's just payroll. It's player payroll," Matt Rhule noted to Dan Dakich. "You look at the National Football League, all the major sports, they all have a salary cap because they say the number one expenditure is paying players. In college football, the spending on players has gone up 60% every year. "What was once a $24 million roster is now a $30 (million). Playoff teams this year, outside research, is about $45 million. Some of the numbers coming out might not have the right word, but some of the numbers are low, it's about $45 million a year.." While Rhule would go on to say that Nebraska has great deals and makes a ton of money from sponsorships and other forms of revenue, it comes down to a decision that the school has to make on where to spend, and how much. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP And yes, there are programs spending the type of money Rhule described. LSU and Texas are certainly on that list. But as college football continues to push the limits — with potential changes still coming through congressional legislation — the cost of building a competitive roster will only continue to rise. Programs with the resources will adapt and find the money. Others will be left trying to compete for conference championships and playoff berths with rosters that cost half as much as the teams sitting across from them. In other words, welcome to college athletics in 2026.

articles.title: 'Game Changer' Anthony Davis Will Be Playing to Get Traded or a Contract, Says NBA Exec
articles.summary: There's belief within the NBA that Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis has his sights set on a new contract or a trade heading into the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
There's belief within the NBA that Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis has his sights set on a new contract or a trade heading into the 2026-27 season.

"It all comes down to him," a Western Conference executive told ESPN's Brian Windhorst . "He's going to be playing for a contract or maybe playing to get traded. He's a game changer."

Washington acquired Davis from the Dallas Mavericks as part of an eight-player swap on Feb. 4, although he didn't appear in a game with the team following the trade due to hand and groin injuries .

The 10-time All-Star will earn $58.5 million for the 2026-27 season before holding a $62.8 million player option for his 2027-28 campaign (via Spotrac ).

While Davis was the subject of trade rumors earlier this offseason, Wizards general manager Will Dawkins is reportedly a fan of the veteran and is not interested in moving him.

Still, Davis has yet to sign an extension with Washington.

According to Josh Robbins of The Athletic, any "meaningful talks" between Davis and the Wizards regarding a possible extension "will occur during the 2026-27 season, not before."

It's understandable that Washington wants to see the 33-year-old on the floor before negotiating a deal given his injury history, as he's appeared in just 71 of a possible 164 games over the past two seasons combined.

Davis has remained an imposing two-way force when healthy, though.

In 20 games with the Mavericks last season, he averaged 20.4 points, 11.1 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.7 blocks per game while connecting on 50.6 percent of his field goals.

The Wizards are attempting to improve upon a 17-65 finish last season with their new trio of Davis, Trae Young and AJ Dybantsa.

articles.title: NBA Execs Vote and Sound Off on Dybantsa, Peterson, Boozer, Caleb Wilson's Rookie of the Year Race
articles.summary: The NBA's 2026-27 Rookie of the Year race is expected to be a competitive one.
articles.body:
The NBA's 2026-27 Rookie of the Year race is expected to be a competitive one.

It isn't a surprise that AJ Dybantsa is viewed as a top contender for the award after the Washington Wizards selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 draft.

"You're overthinking it if you don't pick A.J.," an Eastern Conference scout told ESPN's Brian Windhorst . "He's the most equipped to win the award. Last year, Kon [Knueppel] had a great opportunity, and he had a case but, you know, Cooper [Flagg] was best equipped, and he won it in the end."

Utah Jazz guard Darryn Peterson's outlook for the honor wasn't as certain despite his status as the No. 2 overall pick. He could operate in a smaller role as part of a Jazz starting lineup that also includes Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Keyonte George.

"Rookie of the Year is an award that's centered on opportunity," a Western Conference executive told Windhorst. "[Peterson] is going to be great, but on that team I'm not sure how much opportunity he's going to get."

Meanwhile, Memphis Grizzlies forward Cameron Boozer should receive plenty of opportunities to operate as the team's offensive engine during his rookie season after he was taken with the No. 3 pick.

"Boozer is a winner and he's won things his entire young life," an Eastern Conference executive said to Windhorst. "Memphis isn't going to have a good year, but he's going to be the bright spot and he's going to win the award."

The Grizzlies traded Jackson to the Jazz on Feb. 4 before sending Ja Morant to the Portland Trail Blazers in a June 29 swap , leaving Boozer as their key building block moving forward.

Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson is also playing on a squad that has an eye on the future and could find success under new head coach Tiago Splitter.

"Wilson looked awesome when we got into the film," an Eastern Conference assistant coach said. "He's got all the tools and I have to assume [Bulls coach] Tiago [Splitter] is going to lean into what he can do."

The No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 draft is coming off an impressive Summer League run in which he averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game while shooting 50.0 percent from the field and 41.9 percent from behind the arc.

articles.title: España - Portugal en directo | Última hora de las Ventanas FIBA hoy en vivo
articles.summary: Lo dejamos por aquí. Ha sido un placer estar ahí con vosotros, y nos vemos dentro de tres días para, ojalá, poder ver una victoria de España que certi
articles.body:
Última hora del España - Portugal en directo:

¡Hola, muy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a esta segunda fase de las Ventanas de clasificación FIBA ! España tiene hoy el primero de los partidos para asegurar esa plaza que da acceso a la Copa del Mundo de Qatar 2027 . Tras la primera fase casi inmaculada que finalizó en el pasado mes de julio, los de Chus Mateo vuelven a las pistas para culminar el trabajo que tan bien encaminado tiene.

Con un balance de 5 victorias y 1 sola derrota , España afronta líder este segundo grupo en el que se arrastran los resultados, y donde se cruzará ahora con Portugal y Grecia . Hoy, desde las 21.00 , en el Pabellón Príncipe Felipe de Zaragoza , la Selección española disputa el primero de estos dos encuentros claves contra la selección lusa .

Un Chus Mateo que, poco a poco, va incorporando a los jugadores NBA y Euroliga , liderados por la nueva camada de jóvenes que insuflan un torrente de aire fresco a esta nueva generación, entre los que destaca el debut de Aday Mara y Baba Miller con la absoluta.

También se suma a esta convocatoria el nuevo jugador de los Dallas Mavericks, Sergio de Larrea , y en la que se mantienen otros noveles como Saint-Supéry , Cárdenas o Hugo González . Una lista que se complementa con los más veteranos de la plantilla como los Hernángomez , Brizuela , Parra o Pradilla . Aday Mara , nuevo pívot de los Oklahoma City Thunder , ya confesó en una entrevista para MARCA que "la generación que viene enamora un montón" . Y esta noche, desde aquí, viviremos el inicio de esta nueva era que, esperemos, nos de muchas alegrías .

articles.title: New NBA Expansion Rumors on Las Vegas, Seattle and Latest Prices for Each Team
articles.summary: Amid all of the current NBA franchises being sold at astronomical prices, the cost for potential expansion teams in Las Vegas and Seattle is only going up.
articles.body:
Amid all of the current NBA franchises being sold at astronomical prices, the cost for potential expansion teams in Las Vegas and Seattle is only going up.

Per The Athletic's Mike Vorkunov , groups interested in bringing an expansion NBA franchise to Vegas have been asked by the league to submit a "more detailed portfolio" before a second bidding deadline scheduled for some time in September.

It was previously reported in March that the NBA expects bidding in the "$7-to-$10 billion range" for both Las Vegas and Seattle expansion teams.

Michael Jordan expected to leave media role

According to Vorkunov, some within the NBA have floated $9 billion as the price point for Las Vegas. Seattle would be "expected to draw less" than Vegas in expansion fees.

Vorkunov noted there is belief that the league will select an owner for the Las Vegas franchise before moving onto Seattle, which currently only has one bidding deadline at this point.

There is a board of governors meeting set to take place in September, though it's unclear if there will be any movement on expansion at that point.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver told reporters at the Summer League in July that the league remains on track to make a decision about expansion by the end of 2026, with multiple groups making pitches for Las Vegas and Seattle.

Vorkunov cited several sources who feel Nancy Walton Laurie, an heir to the Walmart fortune, and her husband, Bill Laurie, are the frontrunners to win the bidding for the Las Vegas franchise, but that's not considered a consensus opinion.

Bill Foley, majority owner of the Vegas Golden Knights, is also viewed as a strong contender for the NBA franchise.

Speaking to Vorkunov in July about his pursuit of an NBA team in Vegas, Foley touted the Golden Knights' success with one Stanley Cup title in three Final appearances in their first nine seasons as evidence he would do well.

"We did a couple things really well," Foley said. "We're going to do it on steroids with an NBA team."

Samantha Holloway, majority owner of the Seattle Kraken, hired JPMorgan Chase and Moelis & Co. in May to help advise and structure a bid to bring an NBA team back to the city. She is the only known bidder for the Seattle franchise, but Silver has suggested there are others involved who have not been made public.

A $9 billion price tag for a Las Vegas expansion franchise would make it the second-most expensive NBA club sale behind the Los Angeles Lakers.

Mark Walter recently agreed to sell his majority stake in the Lakers at a $12.5 billion valuation.

In February, CNBC's Michael Ozanian ranked all 30 NBA teams by franchise values with the Lakers ($10 billion), Golden State Warriors ($10.8 billion) and New York Knicks ($10.1 billion) being the only clubs worth more than $9 billion.

Las Vegas has never had an NBA franchise, but the Aces are one of the most successful teams in the WNBA with three championships in the last four years.

Seattle has been without an NBA team since the SuperSonics relocated to Oklahoma City after the 2007-08 season. The WNBA has operated in the city since the Storm debuted in 2000.

articles.title: 4-time NBA Champion raves about Caleb Wilson
articles.summary: Caleb Wilson captured hearts nationwide playing basketball at UNC. The now-Chicago Bull recently earned a pretty impressive NBA comparison.
articles.body:
Basketball superstar Caleb Wilson started turning heads ever since he stepped onto UNC's campus, even when he isn't playing.

Wilson initially chose the Tar Heels over Kentucky , giving former head coach Hubert Davis his greatest recruiting victory. That decision proved to be instrumental for North Carolina, which went a perfect 18-0 at home, while Wilson became arguably the best player in college hoops.

Wilson continued showcasing himself worthy of the Chicago Bulls ' fourth overall pick, setting an NBA Summer League debut record for points . Wilson played so well that Horace Grant, a 7-time NBA Champion and former Michael Jordan Bulls teammate, compared Wilson to franchise legend Derrick Rose.

"Oh my goodness, man," Grant said in a recent Action Network interview, via Rookie Wire's Mack Baltes. "What a beast. What a freakin' beast. He has all the intangibles, the skillset. But what I love about him is that he has the mindset of a killer. A dog. He goes out and gets it. It's one of the best draft picks since Derrick Rose. I'm not going to put him with MJ (Michael Jordan) and myself and Pip (Scottie Pippen), but since Derrick Rose, one of the greatest choices the Bulls have made, in my humble opinion."

Grant, the 1987 ACC Player of the Year with Clemson , won the 1991-1993 NBA Championships alongside MJ and Scottie Pippen.

Wilson ended his lone season at UNC with First-Team All-ACC and All-Rookie Team honors , nearly averaging a double-double with 19.8 points and 9.4 rebounds per game. The Tar Heels looked like a National Championship contender until Wilson injured himself, first in a loss to Miami (FL) and second leading up to the March 7 rematch with Duke .

Against quality competition in the Summer League, Wilson showed early flashes of the same greatness he displayed at North Carolina. Is the Windy City ready for pro Wilson?

articles.title: Heat’s Keshad Johnson not alone when it comes to stepping back (66% pay cut) to two-way deal
articles.summary: MIAMI — Although rare, Keshad Johnson’s shift from a standard contract with the Miami Heat to a two-way deal with the team has NBA precedent. With the move,...
articles.body:
MIAMI — Although rare, Keshad Johnson's shift from a standard contract with the Miami Heat to a two-way deal with the team has NBA precedent.

With the move, Johnson's salary not only goes from last season's $2 million to $678,882 for the coming season, but along with the 66% pay cut, he now only can be on the standard roster for 50 of the regular season's 82 games, ineligible for the playoffs.

The Heat previously have utilized the approach to continue ongoing development with a prospect, taking the same approach during what has proven to be an enduring relationship with guard Dru Smith .

A constant with the Heat since adding Johnson undrafted out of Arizona in 2024 has been the respect of the coaching staff.

"Everybody roots for him because he's so pure," coach Erik Spoelstra has said. "He really works at it. He stays ready so he doesn't have to get ready."

Teams are allowed to carry up to three two-way players, able to swap out those roster spots at any time, with the salaries not counting against the salary cap, luxury tax or hard cap.

Among NBA players who previously have taken the step back from standard deals to two-way contracts is a group that includes former Heat prospect Micah Potter. Others who also have accepted the shift to the lesser, two-way deals after previously securing full-salary standard contracts have been Keaton Wallace with the Atlanta Hawks, Trevelin Queen with the Orlando Magic, Lester Quinones with the Golden State Warriors, JT Thor with the Washington Wizards and Kessler Edwards with the Dallas Mavericks.

Two-way contracts are limited to players with three or fewer seasons of NBA service, with Johnson entering his third season in the league.

Players on two-way contracts can be converted at any time to standard deals without having to clear NBA waivers, leaving that door again open for Johnson.

With Johnson under contract, it also should make it easier for the NBA to allow him to defend his Slam Dunk championship during 2027 All-Star Weekend in Phoenix.

Johnson has shown ongoing appreciation during each step with the Heat. as uneven as the pathway has been.

"Throughout my career," he has said, "I want to keep making an emphasis that I'm willing to do everything, that I'm gritty. I want that to be my identity. I want to make an example of how much of a Heat Culture guy that I am. I really mean it."

With Thursday's signing of free-agent center Nick Richards , it put the Heat's standard roster at 14 under contract, the number required to begin to sign players to Exhibit 10 tryout contracts.

Up first for the Heat was undrafted Louisville forward J'Vonne Hadley, who was a starter on the Heat's summer-league team.

Players on Exhibit 10 contracts can be converted to two-way contracts, potentially putting Hadley in competition in training camp with Heat two-way players Johnson, Vlad Goldin and Tre Donaldson. Teams are allowed to carry a maximum of three players under two-way contracts.

Players on Exhibit 10 contracts also can be funneled to team's G League affiliates, with nominal guarantees. The Heat's G League affiliate, the Sioux Falls Skyforce announced their season will open Nov. 7.

articles.title: Coachella Valley Lakers release schedule, will debut on Nov. 6
articles.summary: This will be the inaugural season in the desert for the Los Angeles Lakers developmental team that will play at Acrisure Arena
articles.body:
The inaugural season of the Coachella Valley Lakers, the NBA G League affiliate of the Los Angeles Lakers , now has a roadmap as the team revealed its schedule for the 2026-27 season on Friday.

The first-ever game for the CV Lakers will be Friday, Nov. 6 at Acrisure Arena against the Salt Lake City Stars. In all, the CV Lakers will play 24 home games from November to March with the final regular season home game coming on Wednesday, March 18.

All home weeknight games will begin at 7 p.m. while Sunday game times are set for a 3 p.m. tip-off. The breakdown by month shows six home games in November, just two in December, six in January, seven in February and three in March.

The roster, and even the head coach, of the Coachella Valley Lakers are still not known, but fans now know when they can see their new home-town pro basketball team play. The team was known as the South Bay Lakers last year and played their home games in Los Angeles.

Fans can already purchase season tickets and individual game ticket sales will be available soon.

There are 31 NBA G League teams, one for each of the 30 NBA teams and one from Mexico City. The CV Lakers will host that Mexico City team on Feb. 25-26. In all, the CV Lakers will host 12 of the 31 G League teams, including Salt Lake City (Jazz affiliate), San Diego (Clippers), Stockton (Kings), Rip City (Trail Blazers), Valley (Suns), Oklahoma City (Thunder), Santa Cruz (Warriors), Texas (Mavericks), Motor City (Pistons), Memphis (Grizzlies) and Rio Grande Valley (Rockets).

Acrisrue Arena, which is in Palm Desert and opened in 2022, seats about 11,000 fans for basketball. articles.title: Awa Fam y María Conde inician el desembarco WNBA en la selección femenina
articles.standfirst: Dos de los puntales del equipo han llegado este viernes y se incorporarán también Raquel Carrera, Alicia Flórez y Megan Gustafson
articles.summary: Dos de los puntales del equipo han llegado este viernes y se incorporarán también Raquel Carrera, Alicia Flórez y Megan Gustafson
articles.body: Antes de afrontar los dos últimos amistosos de cara el Mundial (4 al 13 de septiembre), la selección femenina comenzó a recibir refuerzos. Las primeras jugadoras españolas de la WNBA, que se detiene para la disputa del torneo, llegaron este viernes a Zaragoza para unirse al grupo. Awa Fam y María Conde iniciaron un desembarco que continuará en las próximas horas con Raquel Carrera, Alicia Flórez y Megan Gustafson. "Tenía muchas ganas de llegar a España, de venir y ver a la gente", decía a su llegada una Fam que recibió los calurosos abrazos de Iyana Martín y Elena Buenavida como bienvenida. "Ha sido un viaje largo y estoy un poco cansada, pero estoy muy contenta de estar aquí y de ponerme a trabajar con las chicas y a preparar el Mundial", aseguraba Conde. El objetivo del seleccionador Miguel Méndez es que se integren cuanto antes en la dinámica y en los sistemas del grupo. Apenas hay tiempo Después de haber ganado los tres primeros amistosos, restan dos más. El penúltimo se disputará este sábado (20.00 horas) en Zaragoza frente a Mali, que será uno de los rivales de la primera fase del Mundial. Este domingo (21.00 horas), la selección cerrará los partidos de preparación midiéndose a China, subcampeona del Mundo. El seleccionador tiene a 14 jugadoras tras los descartes de Txell Alarcón y Carolina Guerrero y va teniendo una idea de la lista definitiva. A Berlín se llevará a las 12 que estarán en el Mundial. “Tengo muchas certezas, pero hay diferentes estructuras de equipo posibles, muchas jugadoras en forma. La decisión tiene que ser muy exigente y ellas me lo están poniendo difícil porque puede haber estrellas que se queden fuera”, advierte. Junto al crecimiento del equipo, para el entrenador gallego lo más positivo de las últimas semanas es “la ambición de todas las jugadoras por estar en el equipo final”. Ya huele a Mundial.

articles.title: Cooper Flagg 1-of-1 Rookie Debut Patch Autographed card will sell at auction, rather than owner accepting Mavericks 'bounty'
articles.summary: The Flagg card is expected to sell for millions of dollars at auction, surpassing the $1.1 million Paul Skenes' RDPA card sold for last year.
articles.body:
The owner of the one-of-one Cooper Flagg Rookie Debut Patch Autographed (RDPA) card from Topps has decided to sell the lucrative collectible in an auction, rather than accept the "bounty" offered by the Dallas Mavericks.

Fanatics Collect, which will hold the sale running from Sept. 10-24, announced the auction on Friday . The Flagg card is expected to sell for more than $1 million.

The Flagg card was pulled by Rhode Island collectibles shop Baseball Cards of RI, which opened a 2025-26 Topps Chrome Updates Basketball box during its "RhodyBreakers" live stream on Aug. 10.

Prior to the card being found, the Mavericks offered a considerable "bounty" for the card which included premium lower-level season tickets for 32 years (a nod to Flagg's No. 32 jersey), a signed game-worn Flagg jersey, a post-game photo with Flagg, a VIP tour of the team practice facility and a trip with airfare, hotel accommodations and tickets to see Dallas visit the Boston Celtics, among several other prizes.

The owner of the card, identified as Jason Williams from South Carolina, opted to consign the card with Fanatics and take whatever price is yielded at auction rather than the package offered by the Mavericks.

In a "Debut Bounty Auction," held by trading card marketplace Alt in an attempt to persuade Williams to consign the auction with its company, binding bids for the Flagg card were accepted and went up to $3.8 million before the event was closed on Wednesday, according to The Athletic .

Trading card marketplace Alt attempted to lure the Flagg card to its platform by opening a "Debut Bounty Auction," where it accepted binding bids for the card before it was consigned anywhere.

According to Alt, bids would carry over if the card was consigned to the platform or voided in any other scenario. Bidding had reached $3.8 million for the Flagg Debut Patch before Alt closed the auction on Wednesday.

In addition to the Flagg card, Fanatics will also auction off RDPA cards featuring San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper and Charlotte Hornets forward Kon Knueppel. The cards each feature a patch that the players wore on their respective jerseys during their first NBA games last season.

Last year, a card with a jersey patch from the debut of Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Paul Skenes sold for $1.11 million to Dick's Sporting Goods after it was pulled from a pack by an 11-year-old collector in Los Angeles . That auction was also held by Fanatics Collect.

Baseball players had previously dominated the market for RDPAs. But this past season's NBA rookie class, led by Flagg, is expected to drive significant sales. The Flagg, Harper and Knueppel cards are each expected to surpass the Skenes card in value.

In his first season, Flagg won NBA Rookie of the Year honors after averaging 21 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.9 blocks per game while shooting 46.8% from the field and 29.5% on 3-pointers for the Mavericks.
