articles.title: Todd Golden, Florida Agree to 3rd Contract Extension in 3 Years, Full Details On HC's Deal
articles.summary: Florida men's basketball coach Todd Golden has reportedly had his contract extended for the third time in as many years.
articles.body:
Florida men's basketball coach Todd Golden has reportedly had his contract extended for the third time in as many years.

Golden signed a one-year extension earlier this month that stretched his deal through the 2031-32 season, Mark Long reported for the Associated Press .

He also received a $1.5 million raise that brought next season's salary to $7.5 million, per Long.

His contract is now worth a total of $49.5 million, of which he would be owed 85 percent if fired without cause, Long reported.

Golden is heading into his fifth season with the Gators, which he led to a national title in 2025.

Florida is coming off a 2025-26 campaign during which the Gators went 27-8 to win the SEC regular-season title before a third straight trip to the NCAA Tournament ended with a second-round loss to Iowa.

The extension increased Golden's buyout to leave for another college program by $5 million to $16 million through the 2026-27 season, according to 247Sports' Graham Hall .

Golden's buyout to leave for the NBA sits at $3 million over that span, Hall reported.

The adjusted contract also ties Golden to Florida athletic director Scott Stricklin, Hall noted.

Stricklin's departure from his current position at Florida would lead to next season's college and NBA buyouts for Golden dropping to $5 million and zero dollars, respectively, Hall reported.

Golden agreed to a six-year, $40.5 million extension in May 2025 after his team's national title run. That previous extension brought his average annual salary to $6.75 million.

That deal came about a year after Golden signed a two-year extension worth $4.1 million annually in March 2024, shortly after helping Florida qualify for the NCAA Tournament for the first time in three seasons.

Golden's most recent extension brought his salary to an annual average of $8.25 million per year, according to Long.

According to salary data compiled by USA Today , only Kansas' Bill Self, UConn's Dan Hurley and Arkansas' John Calipari are set to make more than $7.5 million next season.

Golden will now rank as one of the highest-paid coaches in college basketball alongside UNC's Michael Malone, who is also set to earn $7.5 million next season.

articles.title: NBA 2K27 Review So Far
articles.summary: So far, new features have put a spotlight on longstanding issues.
articles.body:
Every year, the NBA 2K series, like our favorite NBA teams, teases enough improvements to give us a sliver of hope; a renewed sense of faith that maybe things will be even better than last time. Although that faith was rewarded last year, that hasn’t been the case in the 10 hours I’ve spent with NBA 2K27 so far. While the on-court play does feel better thanks to smoother and more responsive defensive movements, some new features, like MyCareer Eras, are the opposite. Instead, they act like magnifiers, placing a spotlight on issues that have consistently plagued this series, like an ever-growing emphasis on microtransactions. That can turn what should be an energizing session of hoops into a tiring exercise in scrutiny.

Let’s kick things off with the good stuff: the on-court experience. Offense, although it still feels largely the same, has a few new tricks up its sleeve that make it slightly more challenging than last year. For starters, Rhythm Shooting is much less forgiving than in 2K26 since you’ll have to actually hit the green part of your shot meter to make jumpers. Full disclosure: I religiously use the square button to shoot because it’s what I’ve been doing since 2K10. With this change, I've become even more partial to the classic hold-and-release method since there just doesn’t seem to be an incentive to master Rhythm Shooting’s more finicky timing and down-up motion. Of course, there may come a point when I’ll need to really dig into the latter, but today is not that day.

Then there’s the new logic-based Dunk Meter, which, instead of only showing up when you perform Skill Dunks like in 2K26, now appears whenever you drive to and attempt a shot at the rim. The goal, as always, is to hit the green, but it won’t always be that simple, because this feature takes the defender’s positioning into account. That means even if you get a near-perfect release on your way to a jam, a well-timed contest from a towering, highly-rated defender like Zach Edey or Victor Wembanyama could turn it into a miss.

I’ll admit, taking the Dunk Meter into account did take some getting used to, meaning I’ve missed more than a few slams in trying to master it. But after playing several matches, I’ve come to appreciate the greater sense of realism it lends to 2K27. As much as I would want every poster dunk attempt to go in, even a strong and sure-handed player like Giannis can and should get stuffed at the rim every now and then.

That, of course, leads me to the side of the ball that flusters dribblers, causes turnovers, and wins championships. If last year’s defense was a benchwarmer who barely played any minutes, this year it’s the Most Improved Player. As soon as I hopped into a match, the change felt immediate; being near a defender and putting a hand up actually altered a shot! Gone are the dark days when every jumper, even contested ones, felt like they would go in; now that both sides of the ball are balanced, playing through an entire match, at least in the offline modes, feels better than ever.

Now it’s time to head on over to MyCareer’s neck of the woods, with its latest single-player journey, dramatically titled Fire and Concrete. Like always, this tale follows our recurring hero MP, showing his hoops growth in stages from humble high school roots all the way to a career in the pros. Unlike its predecessors, though, this one’s a doozy, spanning 11 chapters – and bigger always means better, right? Right? Oh, if only that were true.

As soon as I jumped into the thick of things, some flaws immediately stood out, beginning with the story itself. Early on, a key plot point is rushed through in an animated vignette instead of actually unfolding in a motion-captured cutscene, as if it were a commercial as opposed to a career-defining incident. It flashes by so fast that I almost missed it, and makes the start of MP’s journey, arguably the most important part, feel like an afterthought.

Then, there’s MP himself, who, so far, has been very hard to root for. It’s like all the personality has been sucked out of this version of him and given to the supporting characters instead. That said, I am still only in the first half of the story, so our protagonist could eventually experience some much-needed personal growth as the rest of it unfolds. But right now, I’d rather be playing as his funny cousin Cam, voiced and mocapped by Vince Staples, who steals the spotlight in every scene he’s in with his quick one-liners and witty comebacks.

Being the narrative nerd that I am, you’d think my biggest frustration would lie with Fire and Concrete’s lackluster story. Well, it doesn't. Instead, what I’ve been most disappointed with so far is MyCareer Eras, a new mode that lets you drop a created player into one of the six significant time periods in the NBA. Sounds exciting, right? I mean, it does on paper. But then you realize that creating more than one custom character means having to begin with a paltry 60 overall rating each time . So, if you want to actually compete in these Eras, you’ll have to either grind out a crazy amount of matches in The City or spend real money to give your characters an immediate boost.

You might be asking, “Why don’t you just use your upgraded Fire and Concrete player in Eras?” Well, the answer is I can’t. Once you start a save file in the story mode, that player is essentially locked to the Modern Era. You also can’t switch from one era to another, which means if you want to try out all of the time periods, you’ll need to make six separate characters. Do you see my problem now? I didn’t think it was possible, but with this mode, developer Visual Concepts has somehow made microtransactions even more glaring and obnoxious than ever.

But that’s all just part of the opening tip, dear reader, and there’s still a long way to go before we get to the final buzzer. There’s still plenty I haven’t seen that I’m excited to check out between now and then, including the new mode, MyNBA Legacy, which seems like a throwback to Create a Legend from 2K12 and 13 – not to mention all the changes to The City and MyGM. Don’t worry, I won’t be gone long. Once we reach crunch time after the weekend, I’ll be back like MJ in his last game, ready with my final score.

articles.title: Arranca la era de Pedro Martínez en el Real Madrid: llega el debut
articles.standfirst: El técnico se sentará este sábado por primera vez en el banquillo del conjunto blanco en un amistoso ante el Río Breogán
articles.summary: El técnico se sentará este sábado por primera vez en el banquillo del conjunto blanco en un amistoso ante el Río Breogán
articles.body: Arranca la era de Pedro Martínez en el Madrid. El técnico debuta este sábado (20.00 horas) con el conjunto blanco, que disputa ante el Río Breogán en Pontevedra su primer encuentro amistoso de pretemporada. Después de comenzar los entrenamientos el pasado 18 de agosto, toca ponerse a jugar y comprobar si se nota ya la mano y el estilo del nuevo inquilino del banquillo. La cita supondrá el estreno del técnico, que llegó al cargo sustituyendo a Sergio Scariolo y después de hacer al Valencia Basket campeón de la Liga Endesa con un juego tan vistoso como eficaz. Su fichaje supuso un movimiento de gran calado tanto en el conjunto taronja como en el madridista así como en todo el baloncesto español, impactado por la sorpresa de su fichaje. Para su primer partido sentado en el banquillo madridista, Martínez tendrá numerosas ausencias, pues muchos de sus jugadores están con sus respectivas selecciones disputando las Ventanas FIBA de clasificación para el Mundial 2027. Faltarán los recién fichados Mikael Jantunen, Jaime Pradilla, Max Shulga y Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot. También Facundo Campazzo, Gabriel Deck y Andrés Feliz. Con tanta ausencia, el entrenador madridista tendrá que tirar de canteranos. Los prometedores Fabian Kayser, Rhys Robinson y Pablo Mera tienen papeletas para ir convocados porque sólo hay ocho jugadores del primer equipo: el capitán Sergio Llull, Theo Maledon, Alberto Abalde, Gabriele Procida, Eli John Ndiaye, Chuma Okeke, Olivier Sarr y Edy Tavares. El pívot caboverdiano ha renunciado a estar con su selección en las Ventanas para terminar de ponerse a punto tras haberse recuperado ya de la lesión en la rodilla izquierda sufrida en el primer encuentro de la serie de cuartos de final de la Euroliga ante el Hapoel Tel Aviv. Si juega en este amistoso, sería su primer encuentro en cuatro meses. Tras jugar este encuentro, la pretemporada del Madrid seguirá con un duelo ante el Kosner Baskonia el 5 de septiembre en el I Memorial Urbano González Escapa, que se disputa en el Palacio de los Deportes de León. Después, afrontará el XV Torneo Costa del Sol, que ya es un clásico de su preparación. Ahí se enfrentará a La Laguna Tenerife el 11 de septiembre y un día más tarde se medirá al Unicaja. El Madrid de Pedro Martínez debutará oficialmente el 18 de septiembre, cuando dispute la semifinal de la novedosa Supercopa de la Euroliga frente al Dubai Basketball. Seis días después se volverá a cruzar con el equipo de los Emiratos en el inicio de la máxima competición continental. Y el 27 de septiembre, arrancará la Liga Endesa contra el Unicaja.

articles.title: Royce White shows up to Indiana Fever game in blonde wig amid WNBA Draft pursuit
articles.summary: Royce White attended an Indiana Fever game in a blonde wig as part of his public campaign to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft as a transgender woman.
articles.body: Former NBA player Royce White brought his WNBA Draft campaign directly to an arena Friday night, just days after Enes Kanter Freedom was thrown out of a game. Both White and Freedom have declared for the next WNBA Draft as males. White attended the Indiana Fever’s game against the Connecticut Sun at Gainbridge Fieldhouse wearing a long blonde wig, as seen in photos and video obtained by OutKick. The former first-round NBA pick could be seen inside the arena wearing the wig as the Fever prepared to take on Connecticut. He was greeted with a friendly welcome by fans, as multiple people stopped to shake his hand and take pictures with him. FORMER NBA PLAYER ROYCE WHITE SAYS HE IS DECLARING FOR NEXT WNBA DRAFT AFTER ENES KANTER ANNOUNCEMENT When asked by OutKick why he was there, White said, "All hail Queen Roysha, the queen has arrived, it's great to be here... I'm here because Black trans lesbians matter, and we've always mattered, we've always existed... I'm here to participate and scout some of the competition maybe as well." Freedom’s ejection became a national storyline Sunday night and continued to draw attention after he was banned from future Sky games. CHICAGO SKY OWNER OPENS UP ON ENES KANTER FREEDOM EJECTION, MAKES ANALOGY TO SHOOTING A GUN When asked about Freedom's incident and if fans might also see some "fireworks" with White in attendance on Friday, White responded, "I'm just here to spectate. I'm just here to support the WNBA and support the Fever." Asked what reception he expected from Fever fans Friday, White was unfazed: "Who cares? It’s life, you get one life to live. You’re born, you breathe, you stop breathing, hopefully you give all glory to God … Who cares what the reaction is?" His appearance continued the public campaign he launched earlier this month when he announced his intention to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. White previously previewed the look on social media. White formally declared for the draft in a letter sent to the WNBA league office by his attorney, former Florida congressman Matt Gaetz. The declaration stated that White identified as a transgender woman and claimed eligibility under the league’s new collective bargaining agreement. The CBA states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA," but it does not provide a more specific definition based on biological sex or gender identity. White has made clear that his declaration is intended to pressure the WNBA into explicitly stating whether biological males can compete in the league. "I’m transgender. I’m a woman. I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball, professional basketball, so I’ll be declaring for the WNBA draft in 2027 as well," White previously told OutKick. White has also threatened to pursue a discrimination lawsuit if he is not allowed to compete. Multiple outlets reported this week that White and fellow former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom would not be eligible for the draft. A league source characterized their declarations as "publicity stunts." However, White’s legal team said it had not received a formal determination directly from the WNBA. "The WNBA should preserve all records in anticipation of litigation," Gaetz wrote on social media. He appeared in only three NBA games, all with the Sacramento Kings in 2014.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom's legal representatives file FOIA request related to Chicago Sky ejection incident
articles.summary: AFPI filed a six-page public-records request with the government entity that owns Wintrust Arena after Enes Kanter Freedom's removal from a Sky game.
articles.body: The America First Policy Institute has launched an investigation into Enes Kanter Freedom’s removal from a Chicago Sky game and his subsequent ban from Wintrust Arena. AFPI filed a six-page public-records request Friday with the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, the government entity that owns the arena. The request was submitted on Freedom’s behalf under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act. "Enes Freedom exercised his constitutional right as an American when he attended the WNBA game in Chicago," AFPI chief legal affairs officer Leigh Ann O’Neill said in a statement. "Today, we launched an investigation, seeking critical documents that will assist in our efforts to ensure that public entities are held accountable when American’s constitutional rights are trampled." ENES KANTER FREEDOM EJECTED FROM SKY-FEVER GAME AFTER VERBAL ALTERCATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD Freedom attended Sunday’s game between the Sky and Indiana Fever wearing a shirt that read, "WOMAN noun. adult human female." Sky guard Natasha Cloud approached Freedom’s courtside seat during a third-quarter timeout, leading to a verbal exchange. Security intervened and escorted Freedom from the arena after he stepped toward the court. AFPI’s records request seeks to determine who holds authority over access, security and event operations at the publicly owned facility. The group requested agreements among MPEA, arena operator Oak View Group, the Chicago Sky and the WNBA. It also sought security policies, law-enforcement agreements, records identifying who authorized Freedom’s removal and ban, and documents detailing the arena’s receipt of federal funding. ENES KANTER FREEDOM SENDS LETTER TO WNBA REQUESTING REVIEW OF SKY EJECTION INCIDENT, FULL TICKET REFUND MPEA describes itself as a municipal corporation created by the Illinois General Assembly. Its board members are appointed by Illinois’ governor and Chicago’s mayor. The authority owns the 10,000-seat Wintrust Arena, which operates through a public-private partnership with DePaul University. The records request does not itself establish that Freedom’s constitutional rights were violated. AFPI is seeking documents that could help determine whether the conduct of the Sky or arena personnel can be attributed to a public entity. AFPI asked MPEA to preserve potentially responsive emails, text messages and internal communications while producing records on a rolling basis. No lawsuit has been filed. articles.title: Angel Reese Faces WNBA Suspension for 8th Technical Foul After Carla Leite Contact in Dream-Fire
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese is on track for a one-game suspension pending potential appeal of her latest technical foul.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese is on track for a one-game suspension pending potential appeal of her latest technical foul.

Reese was assessed her eighth tech of the season in the fourth quarter of the Dream's Friday night loss to the visiting Portland Fire.

She appeared to make contact with the Fire's Carla Leite before picking up the foul.

WNBA regulations require players who have received seven technical fouls pay a $1,500 fine and serve a one-game suspension for each additional tech.

Reese had earlier in the game tied Alyssa Thomas for the WNBA's single-season record for double-doubles with her 28th of the season.

She finished out the contest having shot 5-for-14 with 16 points and 16 rebounds.

Reese also reached the technical foul limit last season while playing for the Chicago Sky.

She served out that suspension in the fourth-to-last game of a season in which the Sky had already been eliminated from playoff contention.

The Dream are in a notably different position after clinching a playoff spot last Saturday following a win over the Phoenix Mercury in which Reese scored a career-high 31 points.

Atlanta is now in a tight race with multiple clubs including the Las Vegas Aces and Indiana Fever for better playoff seeding.

The Dream already took a step back in that race after conceding a Friday loss to the Fire while the Fever won their own matchup the same night against the Connecticut Sun.

The team may now also be without its top rebounder for Sunday's matchup against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx. A squad led by Olivia Miles, Kayla McBride and Napheesa Collier will be taking on the Dream after putting together an WNBA-best 31-8 record.

The Dream will have to wait to see if the WNBA rescinds Reese's foul before Sunday's game against the No. 1 seed tips off at 3 p.m. ET in College Park.

The Dream, who closed as a 12.5-point favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook, fell 101-83 to the Portland Fire.

In the defeat, Reese tied Alyssa Thomas' single-season record of 28 double-doubles.

Reese and the Dream played from behind for most of the night against the expansion side.

Portland jumped out to a 28-18 advantage and never let go of the lead.

Reese had another productive individual night with 16 points, 16 rebounds and six assists.

Reese recorded her sixth double-double in a row and second against Portland this season.

She was also active in the assist department with six helpers. She's had six or more assists in three of her last six games.

Eight of the 16 boards pulled down by Reese came on the offensive side of the court.

Reese, Rhyne Howard and Jordin Canada powered a second-half surge on offense, but it was not enough for the Dream to pull back ahead of the Fire.

Reese also picked up her eighth technical foul of the season in the defeat. That means she is suspended for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Lynx unless it is rescinded.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Makes History, Sophie Cunningham's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Fever Beat Sun
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever defeated the Connecticut Sun 111-91 on Friday night in Indianapolis, behind a standout combination from Clark and Kelsey Mitchell.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever defeated the Connecticut Sun 111-91 on Friday night in Indianapolis, behind a standout combination from Clark and Kelsey Mitchell.

Indiana entered the matchup as a heavy 17.5-point favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook and lived up to the hype, led by a double-double from Clark with 34 points on 50 percent from 3-point range and 12 assists.

With the postseason field set, the Fever continue their battle for a top-three seed in the playoff bracket with the Dream, Las Vegas Aces, Golden State Valkyries and Minnesota Lynx.

Indiana sits fourth in the league standings at 26-14. The No. 1 seed is likely out of reach for the Fever, but the No. 2 and 3 seeds are well within reach.

Despite Sophie Cunningham's quiet night offensively, she contributed two rebounds, one steal and one block for the Fever. Mitchell, meanwhile, had a standout performance with 34 points on 63 percent shooting.

At halftime, the Fever led 58-43 after an explosive second quarter in which Indiana outscored the Sun 39-15. Clark led the team with 18 points and seven assists, while Mitchell added 17 points.

The Sun's Diamond Miller led Connecticut into the break with 17 points, three rebounds and two assists.

Despite cutting the deficit to 11 points with 4:39 remaining in the fourth quarter, the early deficit proved too much for the Sun to overcome.

The Fever held on for the win and now face a lengthy break before returning to action against the Toronto Tempo on Friday, Sept. 18, on the road.

articles.title: Angel Reese ties Alyssa Thomas for most double-doubles in WNBA single-season history but now faces 1-game suspension after latest tech
articles.summary: Earlier this week, Reese, a three-time All-Star, set the W's single-game and single-season rebounding records with a 26-board performance.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese rebounded from a scoreless first quarter Friday night against the Portland Fire to notch her 28th double-double of the 2026 campaign, tying Phoenix Mercury frontcourt standout Alyssa Thomas for the most in single-season WNBA history.

That said, she shot only 5 of 14 in a 101-83 defeat and picked up her eighth technical foul, which triggers an automatic one-game suspension from the league unless the foul is rescinded.

Reese, who finished with 16 points and 16 boards, was T'd up in the fourth quarter after she and Fire guard Carla Leite were tangled up in the lane.

A player or coach receiving their eighth technical foul during a WNBA regular season results in a one-game suspension, per league rules. Every technical beyond that threshold comes with a $1,500 fine. And every two additional regular-season technicals following the eighth carry another one-game suspension.

Last season with the Chicago Sky, Reese served a one-game suspension once she was administered her eighth technical . This time around, she's set to miss Sunday's home game against the Minnesota Lynx.

While the technical, poor shooting numbers and game outcome poured some water on her recent hot streak, Reese still made some more history Friday night.

Four days earlier, she set the W's single-game and single-season rebounding records in Los Angeles with a 26-board performance during a victory over the Sparks . And now she shares the single-season double-double title with Thomas.

Thomas, a six-time All-Star, logged her 28 double-doubles in 2023 with the Connecticut Sun. Along the way, she piled up double-digit points and assists 11 times. Six of those outings featured triple-doubles (no other WNBA player has more than five triple-doubles all-time, and Thomas has 22 and counting for her career ).

All of Reese's double-doubles this season have resulted from her scoring 10-plus points and mounting 10-plus rebounds, the first of which came in her Dream regular-season debut . It's worth noting, however, that she's stacked at least five assists in five of her double-doubles. On Friday, she added six helpers to her stat line.

Notably, she sniffed a triple-double last week in a road win over the Sparks that saw her amass 20 points, 10 rebounds and 8 assists. That night, she shot 9 of 9 from the field, including 2 of 2 from beyond the arc, and her Dream rewrote a single-game franchise record with 124 points .

Reese scored a career-high 31 points this past Saturday while helping Atlanta take down Thomas' Mercury on the road . The Dream clinched a playoff berth in the process.

The 24-year-old three-time All-Star has elevated her game in her first season with the Dream, who acquired the LSU product in a trade with the Sky this spring . She's averaging north of 16 points per game, and she entered Friday with a league-leading 12.4 rebounds per game.

Unfortunately for Reese, it looks like she'll have to sit out a game before getting an opportunity to surpass Thomas and return to her stat-sheet stuffing ways.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama Scores 22 In First Official Game As France Captain
articles.summary: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama scored 22 points in 21 minutes as France beat Slovenia 92-67 in his first official game as national team captain.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama scored 22 points in 21 minutes Thursday in his first official game as captain of the French national team. France beat Slovenia 92-67 at Bercy Arena in Paris to open the second round of 2027 FIBA World Cup European Qualifiers.

The San Antonio Spurs center added 9 rebounds and 1 block. He shot 5-of-5 inside the arc, 1-of-5 from 3-point range, and 9-of-10 from the free-throw line, and his 24 efficiency rating was the highest of any player in the game.

Rudy Gobert finished with 9 points, 7 rebounds, and 2 blocks. Matthew Strazel had 13 points, 3 rebounds, and 6 assists. Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud scored 13 points in under 10 minutes off the bench. Tibor Mirtic led Slovenia with 9 points and 8 rebounds.

France scored 31 points in the first quarter and never trailed.

"We worked well, we took the game seriously. We approached every quarter the way we needed to. It wasn't perfect, but it was good," Wembanyama said in an interview with L'Equipe .

"When we attack the basket like that from the start of the game," Wembanyama continued, "there isn't much they can do. Physically, we have qualities that they don't necessarily have. We played together."

A 12-0 run bridging the first and second quarters pushed the lead into double figures for good, and France led 54-35 at halftime. The margin reached 31 points in the third quarter. Slovenia closed with a 13-0 run spanning the third and fourth. Announced attendance was 15,831.

France had carried that same 54-35 lead into halftime against Serbia on Sunday in Orléans, then gave the 19-point advantage back and won 91-90 on Jaylen Hoard's layup at the buzzer.

"Everything depends on the circumstances," Wembanyama explained. "At halftime, we had almost the same score as we did against Serbia in the friendly game. We made mistakes in the previous game that we didn't repeat today. It wasn't perfect. You have to know how to find the right words depending on the context."

Serbia had won the first of the two friendlies 90-87 in Belgrade on Aug. 20. Wembanyama scored 10 points in that game. Nikola Jokić finished with 20 points, 9 rebounds, and 8 assists.

The Bercy crowd chanted "MVP" at Wembanyama during the game.

"It feels good. It shows affection," Wembanyama said.

France's three centers combined for 44 points.

"Who else is going to do it? I'm joking. Who else but me has that responsibility? That was my intention, and everyone responded," Wembanyama said. "Regardless of the rotations, we played with three centers today and the level never dropped. That's good. We're showing more and more that our rotations are consistent."

Wembanyama and Gobert last shared a floor in the second round of the NBA playoffs, when San Antonio eliminated Gobert's Minnesota Timberwolves in six games.

"That's normal!" Wembanyama said. "That's the only direction it's supposed to go. I hope to share the court with him for a long time, for years. It's good. It's a step forward. We're working."

The French Basketball Federation named Wembanyama captain on Aug. 19. Thursday was his first official appearance for France since the 2024 Paris Olympics, where he averaged 15.8 points, 9.7 rebounds, and 3.3 assists. He missed EuroBasket 2025 while recovering from a blood clot in his right shoulder.

San Antonio finished 62-20 last season and reached the NBA Finals, where New York won the series in five games. Wembanyama averaged 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists, and a league-high 3.1 blocks in 64 games. He was the unanimous Defensive Player of the Year , made the All-NBA First Team, and finished third in MVP voting . He made his second All-Star team and started for the first time.

He signed a five-year, $252 million extension on July 10 that carries a player option in the fifth season.

France leads Group L at 6-1, with its only loss in the group coming against Finland. Slovenia dropped to 3-4. France plays Sweden on Sunday in Stockholm.
